eagles.name: Brian Pugliese
eagles.project: 9 picnic tables and table repairs for Girl Scout Camp Indian Echo

paragraphs: Brian Pugliese built nine new picnic tables and repaired several existing ones for Camp Indian Echo, the Girl Scouts of West Central Florida camp in Hudson. The new tables give campers and troops plenty of sturdy seating around the pavilion for meals, programs, and gatherings.

Brian organized his team to unpack the table kits, lay out the parts, and work in crews to assemble the legs, tops, and benches, then fastened and checked every table before moving it into place. By the end of the day, nine new tables were lined up beside the pavilion, ready for Girl Scouts to enjoy.

eagles.name: Ishaanth Ravichandran
eagles.project: Search and rescue boxes for PSCO

paragraphs: Ishaanth Ravichandran of Troop 77 spent more than a year building wooden training boxes for the Pasco Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit, replacing aging plastic boxes that had deteriorated in Florida weather. The new boxes are designed to help K-9s track live human scent during search and rescue missions or when pursuing suspects.

Deana Hudgins, K-9 training manager with the Pasco County Sheriff's Office, said the boxes conceal a subject so the dogs have to use their noses rather than their eyes. The completed boxes support training for the more than 55 dogs in the unit and were dedicated to the Pasco Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit.

eagles.name: Blake Borree
eagles.project: Bat houses in the Trinity Oaks neighborhood

paragraphs: Blake Borree installed bat houses around the ponds and wooded edges of his Trinity Oaks neighborhood in Trinity, Florida. A single bat can eat thousands of mosquitoes and other insects in a night, so giving local bats a safe place to roost helps the whole neighborhood while supporting Florida's native wildlife.

Blake and his team assembled each bat house onto a tall wooden post, dug deep post holes, and set the posts in fast-setting concrete so the houses stand high and steady near the water and trees where bats like to feed.

eagles.name: Nick Clohessy
eagles.project: Cemetery refurbishment

paragraphs: Nick Clohessy of Troop 77 led a project he called “Restoring Honor” at Pine Hill Cemetery in New Port Richey, a burial ground established in 1916 whose veterans’ section is maintained by American Legion Paradise Post 79. He wanted to honor veterans for their service and sacrifice; both of his parents, as well as his grandparents and uncles, have served or are serving in the Armed Forces. Working with Post 79, Nick and his team cleaned 103 veterans’ headstones, planted new flag markers and flags beside each stone, cleaned the memorial sidewalk, and installed a solar flag light for the cemetery’s flagpole.

In January 2023, while the work was underway, ABC Action News reported that Scouts spent two days washing and scrubbing headstones so the names of those who served would be clear again. Among those buried at Pine Hill is Medal of Honor recipient James Huff, a veteran of the Indian Wars.
The project was nominated for the National Eagle Scout Service Project of the Year, and Nick received a Community Service Award from the Daughters of the American Revolution.

eagles.name: Dylan Greenwald
eagles.project: Monarch butterfly waypoint at Hospice

paragraphs: Dylan Greenwald created a Monarch butterfly waypoint garden for Hospice. Butterflies need nectar flowers to feed on and host plants like milkweed to lay their eggs on, and Dylan’s garden gives Monarchs and other Florida butterflies a place to stop and refuel, while giving patients, families, and staff something beautiful to enjoy.

Dylan and his team tilled the ground, laid down landscape fabric, set out and planted dozens of butterfly-friendly flowers, then finished the bed with mulch and a good watering. It didn’t take long for visitors to arrive: Monarchs and Gulf Fritillaries were soon spotted feeding in the new garden.

eagles.name: Jackson Davis
eagles.project: Mobile food pantry

paragraphs: Jackson Davis of Troop 77 turned a 2005 school bus into a mobile food pantry for Messengers of Hope Mission, which had been delivering food in volunteers' personal cars. Over two years he raised $16,000 and led 44 volunteers through 450 hours of work: removing seats, building shelves, installing coolers and an awning, and getting the bus ready to serve. When the project was complete, he donated the pantry to Messengers of Hope.
The bus now brings food to families in Pasco and Pinellas counties, including low-income families and people experiencing homelessness. Jackson has said it has been able to serve thousands of people.

In 2023, Jackson received the Glenn A. and Melinda W. Adams National Eagle Scout Service Project of the Year Award. In March 2024, Rep. Gus Bilirakis of Florida recognized the project in the Congressional Record.

eagles.name: Cooper Burden
eagles.project: Repainted part of church

paragraphs: Cooper Burden’s Eagle project gave part of a local church a fresh coat of paint. Cooper planned the work and led a crew of Scouts and adults who caulked and patched the cracks along the beams and trim, cut back overgrown trees, and then sprayed new paint across the walls of the church’s covered walkway.
When the job was done, the whole crew gathered in front of the colorful ocean mural that brightens the courtyard, with a space that looked new again.

eagles.name: Yanni Tsiabasis
eagles.project: Sign/Banner holders for K-Tech. New Port Richey, Florida

paragraphs: Yanni Tsiabasis built a set of sturdy, freestanding banner stands for K-Tech, the Wendell Krinn Technical High School in New Port Richey. The school uses banners to promote its programs at events and around campus, and Yanni's stands give it a reusable, portable way to put them on display.

Yanni started by briefing his team and walking through the design, then the Scouts measured and cut lengths of PVC pipe, glued the frames together with fittings, and test-fit each stand to make sure it stood straight and level. Once every frame was assembled, the team gave them a finish coat of spray paint so they would look sharp at school events.

eagles.name: Evan Knoop
eagles.project: Fire Pit, Hope United Methodist Church, New Port Richey, Florida

paragraphs: Evan Knoop built a fire pit gathering area for Hope United Methodist Church in New Port Richey. The new space, with a stone-ringed fire pit and two sturdy wooden benches, gives the church and its groups a welcoming place to sit around a fire together.

Evan and his team marked out the site, dug and leveled the ground, and laid a brick base inside a steel fire ring before stacking retaining blocks around it. They set the bench posts in fast-setting concrete, checked everything with a level, and built and screwed together the wooden benches to finish the space.

eagles.name: Demetrios Athanasoulis
eagles.project: Shade Structure - St George Greek Orthodox Church, New Port Richey, Florida

paragraphs: Demetrios Athanasoulis built a shaded seating area at Panagia's Playground, the playground at St. George Greek Orthodox Church in New Port Richey. Florida sun can make a playground hard to enjoy, so Demetri's project gives parents and kids a cool place to sit, rest, and watch the fun.

Demetri and his team dug post holes and set tall wooden posts in concrete, checking each one for plumb, then assembled a new picnic table on site. With the shade sail stretched between the posts and fresh mulch underfoot, the new area was ready for families, and the crew celebrated with donuts at the table they built.

eagles.name: Geoff Dziena
eagles.project: Umbrella Stands at the Energy & Marine Center. Port Richey, Florida

paragraphs: Geoff Dziena's Eagle Project was to plan and install umbrella stands at the Energy and Marine Center. Students visit the EMC throughout the year. There are work tables outside where they can touch and feel different items, but these stands have no shade. These new stands will allow the EMC to put out umbrellas when needed to keep the students out of the sun.

eagles.name: Henry Koljeski
eagles.project: Aquaponics Tank at the Energy & Marine Center. Port Richey, Florida

paragraphs: Henry Koljeski's Eagle Project was to plan and install an aquaponics tank at the Energy Marine Center (EMC). This tank will help teach the thousands of students who visit the EMC every year how plants filter the water, the filtered water falls into the tank oxygenating it, and the fish waste fertilizes and is used by the plants to grow.

paragraphs: Noah Ealy's Eagle Project was to plan and install educational signage at the Energy Marine Center (EMC). These signs will allow the thousands of students who visit the EMC every year to easily and quickly be able to identify the wildlife they see.

eagles.name: Atef Alhassan
eagles.project: Outdoor pavilion for Masjid Al-Salaam, Dunedin, Florida

paragraphs: Atef Alhassan managed the location, layout, and construction of a large new outdoor pavilion at Masjid Al-Salaam, the Islamic Society of North Pinellas mosque in Dunedin. The covered steel structure gives the community a shaded place to gather outdoors for meals, events, and celebrations.

Atef started by choosing the site and measuring out the layout on the paver patio with his team. On build day, a telehandler lifted the steel trusses into place while Atef and the crew bolted the posts and base rails together, and the metal roof panels went on top. Finished with wooden serving tables and fresh mulch, the pavilion now seats dozens of guests in the shade.

eagles.name: David Torgerson
eagles.project: Door hardware and wiring at Bishop McLaughlin Catholic High School

paragraphs: David Torgerson's Eagle project took place at Bishop McLaughlin Catholic High School in Spring Hill, Florida, in October 2014. He led a crew of fellow Scouts and adults working on the school's hallway doors.
The team pulled wire through the ceiling to the doorways, worked on the doors' push-bar hardware, and connected the wiring at each door, with everyone in hard hats and safety glasses.

eagles.name: Jordan Groesbeck
eagles.project: Landscaping at Evergreen Woods, Spring Hill, Florida

paragraphs: Jordan Groesbeck led a landscaping project around the buildings at the Evergreen Woods senior living campus in Spring Hill, Florida, in March 2014.
Jordan organized a crew of fellow Scouts and adults, who cleared out the old plant beds along the walls with shovels and wheelbarrows, then dug and prepared the ground for new landscaping.

eagles.name: Zachary Washburn
eagles.project: Fencing at the Tampa BMX track in Lake Park, Lutz, Florida

paragraphs: Zachary Washburn led a project to install chain-link fencing along the Tampa BMX track at Hillsborough County's Lake Park in Lutz. Tampa BMX is a nonprofit track run entirely by volunteers, riders, and their families, and the new fencing helps separate the racing area from the spectator and parking areas.
Zachary organized a crew of fellow Scouts and adults, who unrolled the chain-link fabric, stretched it along the posts and top rail, and fastened it in place section by section.

eagles.name: Zachary Fecanin
eagles.project: Paver area in front of Trinity Presbyterian Church

paragraphs: Zachary Fecanin built a new paver area in front of Trinity Presbyterian Church, turning a landscaped bed beside the main entrance into an attractive, usable space for the congregation and visitors.
Zachary and his team staked and flagged the layout, then cleared and dug out the area with shovels and post-hole diggers to prepare the ground for the pavers.

eagles.name: John Vann
eagles.project: Barbecue Grill Station at Trinity Presbyterian Church of Seven Springs

paragraphs: John Vann's Eagle Project was a barbecue grill station that was completed in February of 2011. This project will benefit the Trinity Presbyterian Church of Seven Springs and the different worship and youth groups that are associated with the church. This barbecue grill will provide an area for the church members to cook food such as hot dogs and hamburgers for different events that are held throughout the year. With the implementation of this project, it will eliminate the need for a parishioner to transport his or her own personal grill to and from these events. It will also eliminate the need for a storage shelter for a propane grill if someone donated one. Its location will also provide easy access for the cooks and workers in the kitchen of the Founder's Hall. The estimated cost of this project is $1,800.

eagles.project: Plan and install a "Walk of Faith" Memorial Brick Pathway for the Trinity Presbyterian Church of Seven Springs
